content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Problem:
To make yourself a color reference booklet, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Purchase heavy-weight watercolor paper (2 hours)
Step 2. Cut the paper into 4x6 inch swatches (45 minutes)
Step 3. Apply a thin layer of clear gesso to the swatches (30 minutes)
Step 4. Punch holes in the corner of each dried swatch (10 minutes)
Step 5. Research different brands of professional acrylics (3 hours)
Step 6. Label the back of each swatch with the pigment code (20 minutes)
Step 7. Calibrate your studio lighting for color accuracy (1 hour)
Step 8. Clean all mixing palettes and brushes (15 minutes)
Step 9. Organize paints by primary and secondary categories (40 minutes)
Step 10. Prepare a set of mixing cups for tints (10 minutes)
Step 11. Squeeze out small amounts of base yellow (5 minutes)
Step 12. Create a spreadsheet to track color properties (2 hours)
Step 13. Print out the color property data sheet (5 minutes)
Step 14. Purchase high-quality synthetic brushes (1 hour)
Step 15. Set up a drying rack in a dust-free area (30 minutes)
Step 16. Sort swatches into the final booklet order (25 minutes)
Step 17. Apply a UV-protective spray to the swatches (1 hour)
Step 18. Test brush strokes on a scrap piece of paper (10 minutes)
Step 19. Mix a series of cool-toned blues (20 minutes)
Step 20. Paint the first row of primary color samples (30 minutes)
Step 21. Measure exact ratios of water for thinning (15 minutes)
Step 22. Clear off a large flat workspace (20 minutes)
Step 23. Paint the yellow-to-green gradient swatches (45 minutes)
Step 24. Select the specific binder rings for the booklet (15 minutes)
Step 25. Sketch a layout for the booklet cover (1 hour)
Step 26. Inventory existing paint tubes (1 hour)
Step 27. Paint the secondary color transition swatches (50 minutes)
Step 28. Review color theory basics in a textbook (2 hours)
Step 29. Let the base layer swatches dry completely (4 hours)
Step 30. Gather reference images of natural light (1 hour)
Step 31. Cut dividers for different color families (20 minutes)
Step 32. Write a short description for each color group (40 minutes)
Step 33. Clean the water jars for the next set (5 minutes)
Step 34. Paint the tertiary color swatches (1 hour)
Step 35. Select a range of warm-toned reds (15 minutes)
Step 36. Design a logo for the booklet cover (2 hours)
Step 37. Thread the swatches onto the binder rings (15 minutes)
Step 38. Apply a second coat of paint for opacity (1 hour)
Step 39. Mix various shades of orange and coral (25 minutes)
Step 40. Glue the swatches onto a sturdy backing card (30 minutes)
Step 41. Label the front of each swatch with the color name (40 minutes)
Step 42. Order a custom-embossed leather cover (3 days)
Step 43. Download a color wheel template (10 minutes)
Step 44. Inspect the swatches for any streaks (15 minutes)
Step 45. Pick up the paper from the art supply store (1 hour)
Step 46. Design the index page for the booklet (1 hour)
Step 47. Print the index and table of contents (10 minutes)
Step 48. Cut the backing cards to size (30 minutes)
Step 49. Check the stock levels of ink in the printer (5 minutes)
Step 50. Press the swatches under a heavy book to flatten (12 hours)
Step 51. Paint the neutral and gray scale swatches (1 hour)
Step 52. Purchase a protective carrying case (1 hour)
Step 53. Mix a set of earth tones and browns (30 minutes)
Step 54. Paint the metallic and iridescent samples (40 minutes)
Step 55. Laminate the index page (15 minutes)
Step 56. Paint the violet and purple swatches (45 minutes)
Step 57. Add a gloss varnish to the finished swatches (2 hours)
Step 58. Sharpen pencils for labeling (5 minutes)
Step 59. Prepare the glue for the final assembly (5 minutes)
Step 60. Refill the printer paper tray (2 minutes)
Step 61. Paint the pastel and light-tint swatches (50 minutes)
Step 62. Mix the final batch of specialty pigments (30 minutes)
Step 63. Wash all used paint rags (1 hour)
Step 64. Create a digital backup of the color data (30 minutes)
Step 65. Photograph each swatch for a digital version (2 hours)
Step 66. Clean the studio floor (30 minutes)
Step 67. Buy a set of fine-liner pens (30 minutes)
Step 68. Paint the deep shadow and black tones (40 minutes)
Step 69. Clean the printer heads (15 minutes)
Step 70. Select the best brushes for detail work (10 minutes)
Step 71. Paint the neon and high-chroma swatches (35 minutes)
Step 72. Draft a "How to Use" guide for the booklet (1 hour)
Step 73. Paint the skin tone and portrait swatches (1.5 hours)
Step 74. Mix the complementary color pairs (40 minutes)
Step 75. Assemble the final booklet pages in the cover (20 minutes)
Step 76. Buy a new set of palette knives (20 minutes)
Step 77. Print the title page for the booklet (5 minutes)
Step 78. Paint the final highlight and white swatches (30 minutes)
Step 79. Apply a matte finish to the divider tabs (1 hour)
Step 80. Sort the paint tubes by opacity (20 minutes)
